title: Lassaigne's Test Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A metal detector finds a hidden coin and bubbles show the hole in a bicycle tube. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) Aarav sees hidden things give visible signals, and chemists find hidden elements in a compound the same way.

You will see carbon and hydrogen detected with copper(II) oxide (lime water turns milky, anhydrous copper sulphate turns blue), then Lassaigne's test live on the molecule bench: sodium gives electrons so N, S and halogens become NaCN, Na2S and NaX ions in the sodium fusion extract. Then the colour tests: Prussian blue for nitrogen, black PbS or violet with sodium nitroprusside for sulphur, blood red thiocyanate when both are present, AgCl, AgBr and AgI for halogens, and ammonium phosphomolybdate for phosphorus. A worked example, the nitric acid trap, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 87 of our PUC Chemistry series. 

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Hidden things, visible signals
0:25 Carbon and hydrogen with CuO
0:50 Lassaigne's test: sodium fusion live
1:30 Nitrogen: Prussian blue
1:46 Sulphur: black or violet
1:58 Halogens: silver halides
2:12 Phosphorus: yellow
2:26 N alone vs N and S, pause and think
2:58 Worked example: read the signals
3:26 Exam trap: boil with nitric acid
3:46 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:21 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Quantitative Analysis of Organic Compounds. We know what is inside, but how much of each?
